frontier.hypothesis: Class B closes if the split copy can be paid for: the 2+2 $s1/$v0 division is proven reachable (H10, cse insns 68/71 on pseudo 75 and 77/80 on pseudo 76), and its ONLY defect is the one extra copy insn that makes the second pseudo join the quantity.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c make_regs_eqv makes whichever pseudo first receives the call result the quantity's canonical register for the whole extended basic block, so a second pseudo can only be introduced by a later copy, and that copy is a real instruction. It cannot be elided: it vanishes only if both pseudos get the same hard register (which destroys the split), and the second pseudo cannot be born free from (set 76 (reg 2)) because C offers exactly one assignment of a call result.
frontier.next_probe: Two ordinary-C routes. (1) Find a byte-neutral 174-insn variant of the floor-9 body ANYWHERE in the function and compose it with H10 (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s7/v/H10.c). s6's D3 was the only 174 ever recorded and s7 disproved it, so this is a fresh search - the tail block, the inner loops, and the sp[] accumulation are all untried for insn count. (2) Find a second pointer whose definition is NOT a copy of the call result but is provably the same address - e.g. a struct member or array element whose address GCC recomputes instead of forwarding - so the second pseudo enters the quantity without a move.

frontier.hypothesis: Class C (rows 62-64) closes if the RTL plus at insn 173 can be flipped to (shift, load) while the row-60 lw of D_800A36A0 stays a distinct in-place memory read.
frontier.mechanism: Pointer-domain PLUS canonicalizes to (base, offset) and keeps the re-read; int-domain PLUS preserves written order but lets cse forward the loop-top base local's register and delete the re-read. E4 keeps the re-read and flips the order but folds 0x6A/0x7E onto the shift operand before the add, costing one insn (176).
frontier.next_probe: Attack the CONSTANT FOLD, not the operand order. Index the row through a struct or array element type so +0x6A is a member offset rather than a folded addend, or give the two inner-loop pointers a common (u8 *)(t0*10) + (s32)D_800A36A0 row whose two users each add their own constant afterwards. Read text1b.rtl (pre-optimization) for E4 (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s6/v/E4.c) and for the baseline side by side; the baseline dump set is in tmp/grind/func_800770B8/dumps/.
